claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 can be processed to contain a hierarchical heterostructure with nanoscale precipitates.
The targeted HfNbTiVAl10 microstructure contains graded phase boundaries.
A multiscale model incorporating nanoprecipitate size and distribution can predict the mechanical behavior of HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately than established simulations.
DFT-derived interfacial bonding energies can be integrated into a continuum model to improve predictions of HfNbTiVAl10 tensile and fracture behavior.
The proposed model can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior with errors under approximately 15%.
The proposed model can complete predictions in hours rather than days.
Hierarchical nanoprecipitates can materially affect tensile yield strength through precipitation strengthening.
Nanoprecipitates and interfacial gradients mediate local stress distributions in HfNbTiVAl10.
Nanoprecipitates and interfacial gradients mediate dislocation nucleation in HfNbTiVAl10.
Nanoprecipitates and interfacial gradients mediate crack propagation in HfNbTiVAl10.
Encoding interfacial-energy variations and nanoprecipitate spacing in scale-bridging laws better captures the dominant deformation mechanisms.
Encoding interfacial-energy variations and nanoprecipitate spacing in scale-bridging laws better captures the dominant fracture mechanisms.
Interfacial-energy variations and nanoprecipitate spacing directly influence plasticity onset.
Interfacial-energy variations and nanoprecipitate spacing directly influence crack growth.
The proposed model will reduce computation time by roughly 70–80% relative to traditional finite-element or molecular-dynamics approaches.
Conventional simulations predict the relevant properties with approximately 20–30% error.
Conventional simulations often require days and extensive empirical calibration.
Unmodeled grain coarsening, phase segregation, or morphological anomalies may reduce prediction accuracy.
Extreme loading rates or environmental conditions may reduce prediction accuracy by introducing additional dynamic effects.
The model is predeclared to be decisively falsified if prediction errors exceed 30% or computation time is not reduced by at least 70%.

contradictions.description: The main prediction requires errors within approximately 15%, but the model is declared decisively falsified only when errors exceed 30%. Outcomes between about 15% and 30% would violate the stated prediction without meeting the predeclared falsification criterion.
